newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian mayor loses uncontested election.
newsitem.headline: Italian mayor loses uncontested election.

text.p: The sole candidate for mayor in an Italian village has failed to win the uncontested post because of voter apathy.
Marcello Cedolin, who was running for re-election as mayor of the small northeastern vilage of Clauzetto, north of Venice, was spurned by many of his fellow villagers.
Only 252 of the village's 639 eligible voters cast a ballot for the incumbent mayor, leaving him short of the minimum 50 percent-plus-one quorum needed to make the election valid.
Cedolin, head of the "Let's Change Clauzetto" electoral list, will now lose his position as mayor and the village will be run by a government-appointed commissioner.
